explanation: Compared with Chowdhury–Sarkis–Shahriari (arXiv:1309.2212, abstract): for n ≥ 4k, every set of n reals with nonnegative sum has at least C(n-1, k-1) k-element subsets with nonnegative sum. The formal statement requires sum exactly 0, which is equivalent: subtracting the mean from each x_i lowers every k-subset sum, so the zero-sum case implies the nonnegative-sum case. nonnegSubsetCount counts k-subsets of Fin n with nonnegative sum; k ≥ 1 is implicit in the source. Faithful.
